The short grievance of the petitioner is that, issuance of the order dated 30.01.2024 vide Ref.No.D.Dis.E/369/2023 by the 5th respondent in violation 3H(4) of National Highways Act, 1956 and also in violation of the provision of The Right to Fair Compensation Transparency in Land, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

2. Heard Ch.Venkat Raman, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Vamshi Krishna, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and E.Kumar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue.
3.

When the matter is taken up for consideration today, Sri Vamshi Krishna, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition submitted that, as there is a rival claim in the present case with regard to payment of compensation, the 5th respondent-Revenue Divisional Officer has an intention to refer the matter under Section 3H(4) of National Highways Act, 1956.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner requested to record the said submissions and prayed to dispose of the writ petition.

In view of the provisions of 3H(4) of National Highways Act, 1956, if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

Now, as per the contention of learned Assistant Government Pleader, as there is rival claim in the present writ petition and the Revenue Divisional Officer has an intention to refer the matter by virtue of provisions referred supra, there is no purpose in keeping the writ petition pending, as such, this Court is inclined to dispose of the writ petition by passing the following order:

"The Impugned order dated 30.01.2024 is hereby set aside and remanded back to the Revenue Divisional Officer for passing appropriate orders by virtue of provisions of 3H(4) of National Highways Act, 1956.
7.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Applications, pending if any, shall stand closed.
